note: Phase 1 exploration (2026-11-02). Names in the practice's own language; English-born practices keep their English names. `script` is the name in its native script where the tradition has one in common use (Pāli is shown romanised: it has no single script of its own). `figure` and `ground` name the exploration's figure and the round-4 ground it sits on.

practices.name: Mettā
practices.desc: Wishing beings well, from the easy ones outward until no one is left out.
practices.note: Sanskrit maitrī. Mettā is the form used on Dharma Seed.

practices.name: Karuṇā
practices.desc: Letting suffering in and meeting it with care; in tonglen, breathing it in and sending ease out.
practices.note: Tonglen (Tibetan གཏོང་ལེན་, gtong len, 'sending and taking') is one practice of karuṇā, so the tile names karuṇā and the description names tonglen. Self-compassion is a modern English practice gathered here.

practices.name: Forgiveness
practices.desc: Loosening resentment, towards others and towards yourself.
practices.note: Contested. Pāli khamā means forbearance and pardon, and Thai and Burmese temples have a ritual asking forgiveness (khamāpana), but the guided practice on Dharma Seed is a modern Western form (Kornfield, Salzberg). Keeping the English name; khamā is an option.

practices.name: Insight Dialogue
practices.desc: Meditating together, in conversation: pause, relax, open, and listen deeply.
practices.note: Born in English (Gregory Kramer, 1990s). The category also holds dyads and other relational practice; 'Relational' stays the search alias.

practices.name: Saṅkalpa
practices.desc: A heartfelt resolve, planted in deep rest and returned to.
practices.note: Pāli saṅkappa is 'intention' in the eightfold path; the practice of a planted resolve comes from yoga nidrā (Satyananda).

practices.name: Samatha
practices.desc: Calming and steadying the mind on one object until it settles.
practices.note: Sanskrit śamatha; Tibetan ཞི་གནས་ (zhi gnas, shiné).

practices.name: Jhāna
practices.desc: The meditative absorptions: joy and ease gathering into deep stillness.
practices.note: Sanskrit dhyāna, which became Chinese chán and Japanese zen.

practices.name: Ānāpānasati
practices.desc: Knowing each breath in and out, in sixteen steps or in one.
practices.note: Sanskrit ānāpānasmṛti.

practices.name: The Mind Illuminated
practices.desc: Culadasa's ten stages, from a wandering mind to effortless attention.
practices.note: Born in English (John Yates and Matthew Immergut, 2015).

practices.name: Trāṭaka · Kasiṇa
practices.desc: Gazing steadily at a flame or a coloured disc, then holding its afterimage within.
practices.note: Two traditions, one method: trāṭaka is a haṭha-yoga cleansing practice; kasiṇa is the Buddhist device (earth, water, fire, colours). Shown together; either could stand alone.

practices.name: Anussati
practices.desc: Recollecting the Buddha, Dhamma and Saṅgha, virtue, generosity and peace.
practices.note: Sanskrit anusmṛti.

practices.name: Vipassanā
practices.desc: Seeing clearly how experience arises and passes, and holds no self.
practices.note: Sanskrit vipaśyanā; Tibetan ལྷག་མཐོང་ (lhag mthong).

practices.name: Noting
practices.desc: Lightly labelling each experience as it comes: rising, falling, hearing, thinking.
practices.note: Contested. The Mahasi method from Burma has no single classical name; Pāli has no term for noting as such. Keeping the English, with Mahasi as the alias.

practices.name: Śūnyatā
practices.desc: Seeing that nothing stands on its own; everything is open, and free.
practices.note: Pāli suññatā. The Sanskrit is the better-known form, through Mahāyāna and Rob Burbea.

practices.name: Maraṇasati
practices.desc: Remembering that this life will end, so that it can be lived.
practices.note: Sanskrit maraṇasmṛti.

practices.name: MBSR
practices.desc: An eight-week secular course of body scan, sitting and gentle yoga (also MBCT).
practices.note: Born in English (Jon Kabat-Zinn, 1979).

practices.name: Open awareness
practices.desc: Resting as awareness itself, with nothing to hold and nothing to push away.
practices.note: No single original: choiceless awareness is Krishnamurti's English; Chinese 默照 (mòzhào, silent illumination) and Tibetan rigpa are close cousins with their own categories. Keeping the English.

practices.name: Zazen
practices.desc: Just sitting (shikantaza), or sitting with a kōan, in the Zen way.
practices.note: Shikantaza 只管打坐 and kōan 公案 are both zazen. Chinese chán 禅, Korean seon are the same family.

practices.name: Dzogchen · Mahāmudrā
practices.desc: Recognising the mind's own nature: open, clear and already complete.
practices.note: Dzogchen (rdzogs chen, 'great perfection') is Nyingma; Mahāmudrā (Tibetan ཕྱག་ཆེན་, phyag chen, 'great seal') is Kagyu. Kin, not the same; they could be split.

practices.name: Ātma-vicāra
practices.desc: Asking “Who am I?” and turning towards the one who is aware.
practices.note: Ramana Maharshi's term. 'Who am I?' (in Tamil, nāṉ yār) is how he put it.

practices.name: Headless Way
practices.desc: Looking back at where your head should be, and finding open space.
practices.note: Born in English (Douglas Harding, On Having No Head, 1961).

practices.name: Effortless mindfulness
practices.desc: Short glimpses of the awake awareness that is already here.
practices.note: Born in English (Loch Kelly), drawing on Tibetan Mahāmudrā's glimpse practice.

practices.name: Nature
practices.desc: Practising outdoors, with land, weather and creatures as company.
practices.note: No single original. Forest practice (Thai thudong, Pāli araññavāsa) is a near cousin.

practices.name: Kāyagatāsati
practices.desc: Mindfulness of the body, from the breath and posture to a slow scan.
practices.note: The Pāli is the classical body contemplation. The body scan itself is modern (U Ba Khin's sweeping, then Goenka and MBSR); 'Body' stays the alias.

practices.name: Caṅkama · Kinhin
practices.desc: Walking slowly and knowing each step: lifting, moving, placing.
practices.note: Caṅkama is the Pāli walking path and its practice; kinhin 経行 is Zen's walking between periods of zazen.

practices.name: Qìgōng · Yoga
practices.desc: Moving slowly with breath and attention: qigong, tai chi, yoga.
practices.note: Ambiguous: the category gathers several traditions. Tàijí 太极 is the other common one. 'Movement' stays the alias.

practices.name: Prāṇa · Qì
practices.desc: Sensing the body as a field of energy, and letting it open.
practices.note: Tibetan རླུང་ (rlung). Rob Burbea's energy-body practice uses English.

practices.name: Kuṇḍalinī
practices.desc: The coiled energy at the base of the spine, rising through the body.

practices.name: Cakra
practices.desc: Resting attention on the body's wheels of energy, one by one.
practices.note: Cakra means 'wheel'; the seven-cakra map is one of several.

practices.name: Yoga nidrā
practices.desc: Guided deep rest, aware between waking and sleep.
practices.note: The modern practice is Swami Satyananda's (1960s); the word is older.

practices.name: Focusing
practices.desc: Listening to the body's felt sense of a situation until it shifts.
practices.note: Born in English (Eugene Gendlin, 1978).

practices.name: Paritta · Kīrtan
practices.desc: Chanting aloud: suttas and blessings, sūtras, devotional song.
practices.note: Ambiguous: paritta (Pāli protective chants) and kīrtan (Sanskrit devotional song) are two traditions. Japanese okyō お経 is a third. Could stay 'Chanting'.

practices.name: Mantra · Japa
practices.desc: Repeating a sacred word or phrase, often on a mālā of 108 beads.
practices.note: Nembutsu 念仏 (Japanese) and dhikr (Arabic) are kin; the tile keeps the Sanskrit.

practices.name: Bhakti · Pūjā
practices.desc: Prayer, offering and refuge, in any tradition.
practices.note: Ambiguous: the category also holds Christian lectio divina (Latin) and taking refuge. 'Devotion' stays the alias.

practices.name: Visualisation
practices.desc: Practising with imagined images: light, deities, places and figures.
practices.note: No single original. Tibetan deity yoga (ལྷའི་རྣལ་འབྱོར་, lha'i rnal 'byor) is the best-known form, but the category is wider.

practices.name: Soulmaking
practices.desc: Rob Burbea's imaginal Dharma: images, eros and soul as ways of seeing.
practices.note: Born in English (Rob Burbea, after Keats's 'vale of Soul-making').
